summary: The article surveys emerging cyber threats to financial data security as of October 2023, including AI-powered attacks, cloud vulnerabilities, cyber-physical threats and Destruction of Service (DeOS) attacks. It quotes several experts and cites example incidents. It then lists defensive steps such as training, zero-trust security, real-time detection, partnerships, policy reviews and endpoint security.
one_line: Overview of emerging cyber threats to financial institutions, such as AI attacks, cloud flaws and DeOS, plus recommended defensive measures.
key_facts: The article is dated around October 5, 2023 and says threats to the financial sector have intensified in complexity and frequency.
On September 15, 2023, a panel of cybersecurity experts, including Dr. Alicia Bell of the Cybersecurity Defense Forum, identified emerging cyber threats for financial organizations.
Dr. Alicia Bell said attackers are exploiting the interconnectedness of financial services, so the potential impact of attacks has grown tremendously.
AI can automate crafting phishing emails that are increasingly hard to distinguish from legitimate communications.
Johnathon Ore, CISO at SafeGuard Finance, said AI-powered threats are a game-changer because they can learn and adapt, likening it to a chess match where the AI is always a few moves ahead.
On September 18, 2023, an international bank lost significant customer data when its cloud-based service provider was compromised.
Consultant Eric Nguyen said strong encryption and access controls are vital for protecting financial data in the cloud.
On October 13, 2023, several ATMs operated by a major bank malfunctioned due to a targeted cyber-physical threat.
Destruction of Service (DeOS) attacks aim to eliminate the backups and safety nets organizations use to recover from a cyberattack.
Laura Kim said on September 26, 2023 that 'never trust, always verify' is the new mantra, replacing 'trust but verify'.
Zero-trust models assume internal and external networks are potentially hostile and require strict identity verification for every person and device.

Recommended steps: training and awareness programs, zero-trust, real-time detection with AI and machine learning, partnerships and information sharing, regular policy reviews, and securing all endpoints.
Mobile banking and remote work make endpoint security more critical, requiring robust encryption, access controls and continuous monitoring.
